column2: On the authority of Abū ʿAmr—and it is also said Abū ʿAmrah—Sufyān ibn ʿAbdillāh (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah,
tell me something about Islam that I will not need to ask anyone else about but you.
He said: “Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.” Reported by Muslim.

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were the most eager of people to learn the religion and the quickest to every good, and this question from Sufyān ibn ʿAbdillāh (may Allah be pleased with him) shows that clearly,
since he asked the Prophet ﷺ this great question, wanting an answer so comprehensive and clear that he would need no one after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ answered this Companion with an answer few in words but vast in meaning, one of his comprehensive statements ﷺ. He said: “Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.”

He commanded him to declare with his tongue his faith in Allah, which includes belief in Him, Glorified and Exalted is He, and in what He has conveyed in His Book and in the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ; so it includes both inward and outward matters,
because īmān and islām are words that divide the meaning between them when they are mentioned together, inward matters going to īmān and outward matters to islām;

but when one of them is mentioned alone, as here, it covers both inward and outward matters. After his faith, certainty and firmness, he was commanded to be upright upon this truth and guidance and to continue in it, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said:

“O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims” [Āl ʿImrān 3:102], that is, persevere in obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger, so that when your appointed time comes, it finds you in a good state.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made clear in His Book the reward of whoever believes and is upright, saying: “Indeed, those who say ‘Our Lord is Allah’ and then remain upright—the angels will descend upon them, [saying]: Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive the good news of Paradise, which you were promised” [Fuṣṣilat 41:30]; and He said:

“Indeed, those who say ‘Our Lord is Allah’ and then remain upright—there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve. Those are the people of Paradise, abiding in it forever, as a reward for what they used to do” [al-Aḥqāf 46:13–14].
The Companions' eagerness to ask about the matters of their religion.
The excellence of Sufyān ibn ʿAbdillāh's question, which shows the completeness of his intellect and his desire for comprehensive advice.
Belief in Allah and in what He has conveyed in His Book and in the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.
Holding constantly to uprightness upon truth and guidance until one's appointed time comes.
